svg.title: When the review is wrong, the fix is rarely in the code it reviewed
svg.desc: Five rows, each naming the place the fix lives, the symptom you see in the review, and what to do. Row one, the ticket or the PR body: a not found on a criterion that is plainly covered means the ticket's wording or Seams line is off, fix the ticket; a first finding of No Closes reference found means the PR body lacks Closes number, add it. Row two, amber, the skill file review-pr SKILL.md: a file and line that does not say what the review claims means add quote the line to the Criteria check; a rule AGENTS.md does not contain means the Standards check must name the rules; a Blocker with the wrong verdict or verdicts that differ between runs means the Severity table is ambiguous, add the case on one side. Row three, amber, the agent file reviewer.json: a refused command in the review text means add one narrow glob to the allow list, never trust all tools; a comment saying the run produced no review means open the run log, usually a refused command retried or a write to the wrong path. Row four, the secret: the step logs KIRO API KEY is not set and exits zero, set the secret in your fork, or review a colleague's PR locally with section five. Row five, red, the workflow ai-review.yml: the review approved or requested changes, stop, git log the workflow file, put the comment flag back before another run. A green strip at the bottom says: first, every time, check the row yourself and rerun once with gh workflow run; edit a file above only when it repeats; the reviewed code is the last place to look.
svg.text: When the review is wrong, the fix is rarely in the code it reviewed
Ten things that come up, sorted by the file that owns the fix. Find the row, then edit that file and nothing else.
WHERE THE FIX LIVES
WHAT YOU SEE
WHAT TO DO
Ticket or PR body
Seams: / Closes #T
not found on a criterion that is covered
"No Closes reference found" as the first finding
The Seams line or the wording is off.
Fix the ticket, as lesson 7 section 7 says.
Add Closes #T to the PR body. Nothing else.
The skill
review-pr/SKILL.md
A file:line that doesn't say what it claims
A finding citing a rule AGENTS.md doesn't have
A Blocker with the wrong verdict, or two runs
on the same commit with different verdicts
Criteria check: add "quote the line".
Standards check: name the rules. No opinion.
Severity table: add the case, on one side.
The verdict is only as stable as the table.
The agent file
.kiro/agents/reviewer.json
A refused command in the review text
A comment: the run produced no review
Add one narrow glob to the allow list.
Never --trust-all-tools.
Open the run log. Usually a refused command
retried, or a write to the wrong path.
The secret
gh secret list
"KIRO_API_KEY is not set", and the step
exits 0 with no review
Set it in your fork. For a colleague's PR into
your fork, review locally with section 5.
The workflow
ai-review.yml
The review approved, or requested changes
The agent can't post, so the posting line changed
Stop. git log -p the workflow file.
Put --comment back before another run.
FIRST, EVERY TIME
Check the row yourself. Rerun once:
gh workflow run ai-review.yml -f pr=<n>
Edit a file above only when it repeats. The reviewed code is the last place to look.
